title: The rule
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting, lonely 1970s roadside motel at night in the rain, buzzing pink neon and sodium orange glow against deep blue darkness, wood paneling and worn carpet, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 1. The motel had one rule. I broke it on a Tuesday. 🔑

Original fiction. Part 2 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: The Bluebell Motor Inn has eleven rooms and one rule. Never rent Room 9.
scenes.image: lonely roadside motel at night in the rain, a flickering neon glow over a row of identical doors

scenes.narration: Marcus Hale took the night shift because nobody else would. Eleven to seven. Free coffee. A radio that only gets one station.
scenes.image: tired man in his thirties behind a wood-paneled motel front desk at night, a coffee mug and an old radio beside him

scenes.narration: The owner, Mr. Dell, said it twice. Doesn't matter who asks. Doesn't matter if we're full. Room 9 stays empty.
scenes.image: stern older man in a cardigan leaning over a motel counter under a dim lamp, pointing one finger

scenes.narration: Three weeks, nobody asked. Then, on a Tuesday, at 1:40 in the morning, a man in a grey raincoat stepped in out of the rain.
scenes.image: a man in a long grey raincoat standing dripping in a motel office doorway, rain and neon behind him

scenes.narration: He didn't look at the key board. He didn't look at Marcus. He just said: Nine, please. I'm expected.
scenes.image: close-up of a wall of old brass motel keys on hooks, one key in the middle glinting in the lamplight

scenes.narration: Marcus said no. Said we had ten other rooms. The man just waited. Rain ticking off his coat onto the carpet. He didn't blink. Not once.
scenes.image: rainwater dripping from the hem of a grey raincoat onto worn orange motel carpet, close-up

scenes.narration: At two minutes to two, Marcus heard himself say okay. He doesn't remember deciding. He only remembers the key was already in his hand.
scenes.image: a man's hand holding an old brass motel key on a plastic fob, warm lamplight, shadows

scenes.narration: The man signed the guestbook and walked to the end of the row. The light in Room 9 came on. It never went off.
scenes.image: row of motel doors at night in the rain, the very last window glowing warm yellow

scenes.narration: At 2 AM, Marcus heard a pen scratching. The guestbook lay open on the counter. Nobody was holding the pen.
scenes.image: an old leather guestbook open on a motel counter at night, a fountain pen standing upright on the page by itself

scenes.narration: A new line was writing itself, slow and careful. A name he couldn't read. And a check-in date. Tomorrow's.
scenes.image: close-up of fresh wet ink spreading across a yellowed guestbook page, illegible handwriting, desk lamp glow
